#!/bin/sh

# Flux directives translated from SLURM
#FLUX: -N 1
#FLUX: -n 1
#FLUX: -t 2:00:00
#FLUX: -q lu
#FLUX: --exclusive
#FLUX: -o lunarc_output/lunarc_output_snre_hp_%J.out

#
# --- Omitted SLURM options and explanations ---
#
# -A lu2020-2-7
#   Omitted. Flux accounting is typically managed through system configuration or job
#   submission options, not a standard batch directive.
#
# -J snre_b
#   Omitted. The job name in Flux is generally set during submission (e.g.,
#   'flux submit --job-name=snre_b ...') or via the FLUX_JOB_NAME
#   environment variable, not through a script directive.
#
# -e lunarc_output/lunarc_output_snre_hp_%j.err
#   Omitted. Flux combines stdout and stderr into the single output file
#   specified by the -o directive. To redirect stderr separately, you can use
#   shell redirection in your command, e.g., 'command 2> ...'.
#
# --mail-user=samuel.wiqvist@matstat.lu.se and --mail-type=ALL
#   Omitted. Flux core does not have built-in support for email notifications via
#   batch directives. This functionality may be provided by site-specific
#   plugins or wrappers.
#
# Note: The original SLURM script did not request any specific amount of memory.
# This job will receive the default memory allocation from the scheduler.
#

# load modules
ml load GCC/8.3.0
ml load CUDA/10.1.243
ml load OpenMPI/3.1.4
ml load PyTorch/1.6.0-Python-3.7.4

# run program
python /home/samwiq/snpla/'seq-posterior-approx-w-nf-dev'/'two_moons'/run_script_snre_b.py 1 2 11 10 8

issues: The script loads CUDA and PyTorch modules, strongly suggesting it is a GPU-accelerated application. However, it does not explicitly request a GPU in its resource directives (e.g., using `#FLUX: -g 1`). While requesting an exclusive node in a GPU queue might implicitly provide access to the GPUs, this is not guaranteed and is poor practice. The job may fail if it cannot find a CUDA device.

The script does not request any specific amount of memory. For a PyTorch/machine learning job, this is a critical omission. The job will receive a default memory allocation from the scheduler, which is very likely to be insufficient, leading to an out-of-memory failure.

The script specifies an output file in a subdirectory (`lunarc_output/...`). If this directory does not exist in the working directory when the job starts, the job will fail because it cannot create the output file.
The script is extremely non-portable and fragile due to the hardcoded, user-specific absolute path to the Python executable, which also contains spaces and multiple levels of quoting.

#!/bin/sh


#SBATCH -A lu2020-2-7
#SBATCH -p lu

# time consumption HH:MM:SS
#SBATCH -t 2:00:00

#SBATCH -N 1
#SBATCH --tasks-per-node=1
#SBATCH --exclusive

# name for script
#SBATCH -J snre_b


# controll job outputs
#SBATCH -o lunarc_output/lunarc_output_snre_hp_%j.out
#SBATCH -e lunarc_output/lunarc_output_snre_hp_%j.err

# notification
#SBATCH --mail-user=samuel.wiqvist@matstat.lu.se
#SBATCH --mail-type=ALL

# load modules

ml load GCC/8.3.0
ml load CUDA/10.1.243
ml load OpenMPI/3.1.4
ml load PyTorch/1.6.0-Python-3.7.4

# run program
python /home/samwiq/snpla/'seq-posterior-approx-w-nf-dev'/'two_moons'/run_script_snre_b.py 1 2 11 10 8
